name: Edward VII cast-iron pillar post box, North Circular Road
address: South side of North Circular Road outside No. 530, Dublin 1
historical_description: Cast-iron pillar box with Edward VII royal insignia, a fluted frieze below the cap, a letter aperture flanked by raised POST OFFICE lettering, and an E VII R monogram with crown motif on the door. The base bears the maker's mark Handyside Derby & London. NIAH records green paint and a black base.
historical_significance: A surviving Edwardian postal artefact that remained in use in the NIAH survey record, retaining royal insignia and a named manufacturer.

name: Victorian cast-iron pillar post box, Mountjoy Square West
address: South-west corner of Mountjoy Square West at Grenville Street, Dublin 1
historical_description: Freestanding cast-iron post box with round plan, shallow domed cap, moulded corona and a single letter slot between two neck mouldings. The curved hinged door bears a raised VR royal monogram; the maker's name is cast in raised lettering as Handyside & Co of Derby.
historical_significance: A Victorian pillar box retaining Queen Victoria's royal insignia and a foundry name, providing evidence of late nineteenth-century postal infrastructure and cast-iron manufacture.
